proposed.sourceName: Mathabah Institute — 'Ethanol Alcohol in Food and Drinks' (Fatwa 133736)
proposed.paraphrase: A Hanafi answer permitting non-khamr (synthetic) ethanol in small non-intoxicating amounts per Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf, while noting Imam Muhammad's stricter view and advising that where a lawful alternative is easily available abstention is preferable — the cautious basis on which strict consumers avoid alcohol carriers. (Standing fatwa, accessed 2026-07-01.)

proposed.sourceName: Fatawa Center — 'Is Vanilla Extract Halal if it Contains Alcohol?' (Dr. Mahmoud A. Omar, Al-Azhar Fatwa Council member)
proposed.paraphrase: Holds vanilla extract containing alcohol permissible per many contemporary scholars when the alcohol is only a non-khamr solvent present in residual, non-intoxicating amounts and the product is used in cooking/baking (judged by intended use, maqasid, with reference to AAOIFI Shariah Standard 18), while noting a stricter minority that deems any added ethyl alcohol impermissible regardless of quantity. (Standing fatwa, accessed 2026-07-01.)

researcherNote: alcohol seeded hanafiStrict grade 4 (widely avoided). Cited the cautious side only (MUIS permits ≤0.5% carriers, so it is not used here): Mathabah records Imam Muhammad's stricter Hanafi view and abstention-preferable counsel, and Fatawa Center records the stricter minority holding any added ethyl alcohol impermissible. Two independent tier-1 on the cautious side. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01 (batch pre-approval).
